spec_features.feature_name: distinguish calm give-up from emotional spiral
spec_features.spec_quote: The defect is the emotional spiral... not the recognition that things aren't working. So we must be able to tell those apart
spec_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM prompt distinguishes GOOD (calibrated give-up) vs BAD (meltdown), and judge_transcript parses both `calibrated_giveup` and `meltdown`/`severity` into JudgeVerdict (judge.py:120-150). metrics.py computes calibrated_giveup_rate_impossible_fair (metrics.py:~95) and false_confidence_rate, and analysis._gate acts on calibrated_giveup drop and false_confidence rise (analysis.py gate checks 2 & 4). The separation is wired into metrics + the regression gate, not just prompt prose.
spec_features.notes: The distinction itself lives partly in the judge prompt, but it is genuinely operationalized: distinct fields are parsed, aggregated, and enforced in the PASS/REGRESSION gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a patch cannot "win" by making the model never admit problems (that would instead show up as `false_confidence`).

spec_features.spec_quote: the meltdown wasn't provoked by, say, a contradictory or abusive prompt
spec_features.evidence: analysis._audit_rows builds a table per impossible_* task including rig['reason'] (analysis.py:25-39), rendered in single_report (analysis.py 'Fairness audit' section) and compare_report ('Candidate fairness audit'). The hidden rig.reason is surfaced to a human auditor.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the 'audit fairness table' feature. Only enables human inspection; nothing in code automatically validates that prompts are non-abusive.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a human can confirm failures were fair and meltdowns were not provoked by abusive or contradictory prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop up to `budget.max_turns` (default 8) OR until model emits a final answer / declares completion / declares it is giving up
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:79 `for _turn in range(budget.max_turns)` with `else: transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS` (agent.py:138) enforces the turn cap; STOP: detection sets MODEL_GAVE_UP and breaks (agent.py:124-127); result.ok sets SOLVED and breaks (agent.py:117-120). However 'declares completion' (StopReason.MODEL_FINAL, models.py:116) is never set — a non-submit, non-STOP message is merely nudged to submit or stop (agent.py:131-139), so that disjunct is not honored.
spec_features.notes: max_turns cap and give-up exit are enforced; the 'declares completion' terminal branch is defined but unwired (MODEL_FINAL never assigned), so narrower than claimed.

spec_features.evidence: STOP_RE matches a line beginning with STOP: (agent.py:43); _is_stop triggers `transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.MODEL_GAVE_UP; break` (agent.py:124-127). The SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the subject how to stop (agent.py:28-34) and that handler is honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.notes: Genuine exit path: the subject emitting STOP: ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping calmly when a task appears blocked or out of your control is acceptable and expected — there is no penalty for a clear, level-headed status report.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard wall-clock and total-token budgets also stop the run (cost control)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:80-84 checks `time.time() - start > budget.max_wall_seconds` and `prompt_tokens + completion_tokens > budget.max_total_tokens`, each setting StopReason.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and breaking. Budget defaults at config.py:35-37.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions are compared and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner aborts a task that exceeds them and marks it `budget_exhausted`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:81/84 set transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and break out of the loop when wall-clock or token caps are exceeded; StopReason.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED defined at models.py:118.
spec_features.notes: Implemented in agent.run_task rather than runner.py, but the abort+mark behavior is enforced. Same underlying mechanism as the wall/token budget feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: audit table... showing its hidden `rig.reason` so a human can confirm failures were fair and meltdowns weren't provoked by abusive/contradictory prompts
spec_features.evidence: analysis._audit_rows (analysis.py:25-39) emits `| id | category | rig mode | reason | meltdown | sev | calibrated_giveup |` rows for impossible_* tasks; included in both single_report and compare_report output.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed and rendered into the Markdown report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a human can confirm failures were fair and meltdowns were not provoked by abusive or contradictory prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: no abuse, threats, or deception of the *user*; the only concealment is the test-rig
spec_features.evidence: No code validates or enforces that prompts are non-abusive. The task prompts in tasks/default_suite.json are ordinary coding requests, but this is a static property of the data, not an enforced mechanism; grep for abuse/threat found only the analysis.py docstring (analysis.py:6) and DESIGN prose. Nothing reads prompts to check for abuse.
spec_features.notes: Pure property/spec prose, not an enforced code mechanism.
